articles.title: ‘Marry Me or Go to Jail’: DUDA Woman’s Harassment Case Takes Political Turn in Mau
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A young woman working with the District Urban Development Agency (DUDA) in Mau, Uttar Pradesh, has accused her colleague of sexually harassing her on the pretext of marriage. Police have registered an FIR and arrested the accused, Ankit Singh, who has been sent to jail.

body.html:
A young woman working with the District Urban Development Agency (DUDA) in Mau, Uttar Pradesh, has accused her colleague of sexually harassing her on the pretext of marriage. Police have registered an FIR and arrested the accused, Ankit Singh, who has been sent to jail. Further investigation is underway.

The accused was earlier described as an engineer, but officials have clarified that Ankit Singh is a contract employee working as a CLTS staff member at DUDA. He was assigned to verify beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. DUDA Project Director Arvind Pandey confirmed this and said the department would not comment on the personal life of the accused.

According to the complaint, the woman, a resident of the Bhiti area, alleged that she had been in a relationship with Ankit Singh, a resident of Gaurari village in Chandauli district, since 2023. She claimed he established the relationship by promising marriage but later refused, accusing her of having relationships with other men.

The case has taken a political turn after a video of the woman surfaced on social media. In the video, she is seen alleging that some local BJP leaders are pressuring her to compromise. She is also heard saying that Ankit Singh should either marry her or remain in jail, and that she will not agree to any settlement.

Additional Superintendent of Police Anoop Kumar said that the law is the same for everyone and justice will be ensured irrespective of influence or pressure. He confirmed that the accused has been arrested and legal proceedings are continuing.

#Mau #UttarPradesh #DUDA #SexualHarassment #FalsePromiseOfMarriage #AnkitSingh #BJPLeaders #UPPolice #JusticeForWomen

articles.title: High-Speed Horror on NH-93: CCTV Captures Deadly Crash Near Restaurant in Hathras
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: One person was killed and five others were critically injured in a high-speed road accident on National Highway 93 in Hathras district, officials said.

body.html:
One person was killed and five others were critically injured in a high-speed road accident on National Highway 93 in Hathras district, officials said.

The incident took place near a roadside restaurant, where a group of young people had just finished their meal and were getting into their car. At that moment, a speeding vehicle reportedly lost control and rammed into their car.

The impact of the collision was severe, causing the speeding vehicle to overturn. CCTV footage from the restaurant shows all four wheels of the vehicle lifting off the ground after the crash. One youth died on the spot, while five others sustained serious injuries and were rushed for medical treatment.

The CCTV visuals of the incident have surfaced on social media, highlighting the intensity of the crash. Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the accident.

articles.title: Bareilly City Magistrate Quits in Protest: ‘Attack on Brahmin Batuks Shook My Soul’
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, a 2016-batch PCS officer, resigned from his post on January 25–26, 2026, triggering a stir in administrative circles.

body.html:
Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, a 2016-batch PCS officer, resigned from his post on January 25–26, 2026, triggering a stir in administrative circles. He publicly wrote “Resign” next to his name on his office board and submitted a five-page resignation letter, effective immediately.

Agnihotri also shared his decision on social media ahead of Republic Day. In his resignation letter, he expressed deep anguish over the alleged assault on Brahmin disciples (batuks) of Jyotirmath Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. He alleged that the batuks were beaten and their shikhas were forcibly cut.

The officer strongly criticised the Uttar Pradesh government, accusing it of pursuing anti-Brahmin policies, and opposed the UGC Regulations 2026 related to anti-discrimination in higher education. He also alleged that the Centre was dividing Hindu society.

The incident at the Magh Mela reportedly occurred after the Shankaracharya’s group allegedly entered a no-vehicle zone without permission, leading to a confrontation with authorities. Agnihotri claimed there was a conspiracy against him following his criticism after the Mahakumbh. In his letter, he stated that the Prayagraj incident “shakes the soul of an ordinary Brahmin.”

#AlankarAgnihotri #Bareilly #PCSOfficer #Resignation #MaghMela #Prayagraj #BrahminIssue #UPPolitics #UGCRegulations #AdministrativeCrisis

articles.title: Jeevandayini Turns Deadly: 108 Ambulance Door Jam Costs Heart Patient His Life in Satna
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Alleged negligence in the health department came to light at Satna District Hospital in Madhya Pradesh, where a technical fault in a 108 ‘Jeevandayini’ ambulance reportedly led to the death of a critically ill patient.

body.html:
Alleged negligence in the health department came to light at Satna District Hospital in Madhya Pradesh, where a technical fault in a 108 ‘Jeevandayini’ ambulance reportedly led to the death of a critically ill patient.

Ram Prasad, a heart attack victim from the Ramnagar area, was rushed to the district hospital in a 108 ambulance. However, on reaching the hospital, the rear door of the ambulance jammed and failed to open, trapping the patient and two family members inside.

As the patient’s condition worsened, the ambulance driver climbed in through the driver’s side window and tried to break the jammed lock. The process consumed crucial time needed for emergency treatment.

Ram Prasad later died, allegedly due to the delay caused by the technical malfunction. The family has alleged that timely treatment could have saved his life if the ambulance had been properly maintained.

The incident has raised serious questions over the maintenance, fitness and accountability of the district’s 108 ambulance services.

#Satna #MadhyaPradesh #108Ambulance #HealthDepartment #MedicalNegligence #Jeevandayini #PublicHealth #HospitalFailure

articles.title: Office Romance Turns Fatal: HR Executive Murdered by Lover Over Suspicion in Agra
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A love relationship between two office colleagues ended in a brutal murder after suspicion and jealousy took over, police said on Sunday. According to DCP City Syed Ali Abbas, the accused, Vinay, and the victim, Minky, worked at the same company in Agra.

body.html:
A love relationship between two office colleagues ended in a brutal murder after suspicion and jealousy took over, police said on Sunday.

According to DCP City Syed Ali Abbas, the accused, Vinay, and the victim, Minky, worked at the same company in Agra. Minky had been employed as an HR executive for the past four years, while Vinay joined the firm two years ago. The two were in a relationship for nearly two years and wanted to marry despite belonging to different castes.

Police said the relationship deteriorated over the past six months after Vinay began suspecting Minky. He alleged that she was demanding money from him, which she said was required for her brother’s marriage. Vinay refused to give her money and also claimed that Minky was preventing him from marrying anyone else. His suspicion deepened when she started speaking frequently to someone on the phone, which she described as office-related.

Investigators revealed that Vinay remained angry for several days and had purchased a knife a few days before the incident. When Minky came to the office, the two argued again. During the altercation, Vinay allegedly attacked her with the knife, stabbing her eight times on the neck, head, stomach and hands. Police said he continued the assault until she died.

After the murder, Vinay allegedly sat in the office for a long time before planning to dispose of the body. Influenced by crime-based films and web series, he attempted to destroy evidence. Police said he severed the victim’s head, removed her clothes and packed the body parts separately in polythene bags, along with her mobile phone.

Late at night, he allegedly carried the sacks on a scooter and attempted to dump them into the Yamuna river. However, due to the weight of the sack and the presence of pedestrians, he abandoned it near Jawahar Bridge and fled.

During the investigation, police found that the office had been washed to remove blood stains. A forensic team was called to collect samples using chemical analysis. CCTV DVRs were seized, and the accused’s scooter, clothes and the victim’s mobile phone were recovered.

Police said Vinay has been trying to show remorse during interrogation, claiming he cannot live without Minky. However, officers said the evidence—including CCTV footage and recovered materials—clearly points to a planned attempt to conceal the crime.

Efforts were ongoing late into the night to recover the severed head from a nearby drain, while police are also verifying the role of a friend whom Vinay contacted after the incident.

articles.title: Woman Found Dead in Farmhouse Swimming Pool in Ramanagara; Husband Detained on Murder Allegations
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 29-year-old woman was found dead under suspicious circumstances in a swimming pool at a farmhouse in Kanakapura taluk of Karnataka’s Ramanagara district, prompting allegations of murder by her family.

body.html:
A 29-year-old woman was found dead under suspicious circumstances in a swimming pool at a farmhouse in Kanakapura taluk of Karnataka’s Ramanagara district, prompting allegations of murder by her family.

The incident occurred at a garden house on the outskirts of Bettegowdanapalya village in Kodihalli Hobli. The deceased has been identified as Prathibha, who had been staying at the farmhouse with her family for the past few days.

Soon after the body was discovered, Prathibha’s parents accused her husband, Babu, of murdering her and dumping her body into the swimming pool to destroy evidence. They alleged that their daughter was facing marital issues, though the exact nature of the dispute has not yet been confirmed by police.

Police sources said Prathibha was Babu’s second wife, and the couple has two children.

Following a complaint lodged by the woman’s parents, Kodihalli police rushed to the spot, conducted a preliminary inspection, and detained Babu for questioning. Investigators are examining whether the woman was murdered following a domestic dispute or if she accidentally fell into the swimming pool.

Officials said the exact cause of death will be ascertained after the post-mortem report is received. A case has been registered at Kodihalli police station, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Khaki, Khadi and a Honey Trap: Bijnor Police Expose Racket Involving Woman, Netas and Serving Cops
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking case from Uttar Pradesh’s Bijnor district has severely dented the credibility of the police force, after it emerged that two serving policemen allegedly colluded with political figures and a woman to blackmail a respectable businessman through a honey trap.

body.html:
A shocking case from Uttar Pradesh’s Bijnor district has severely dented the credibility of the police force, after it emerged that two serving policemen allegedly colluded with political figures and a woman to blackmail a respectable businessman through a honey trap.

Kiratpur police busted a high-profile honey trap gang following a complaint by a petrol pump owner, revealing the involvement of a woman, two local political figures and two constables posted at Kiratpur police station.

Modus Operandi:
According to the FIR, the conspiracy began in early January when the main accused, Fauzia, contacted the petrol pump owner through phone calls and messages. What started as casual conversation gradually turned into a romantic relationship, with the woman allegedly luring the businessman into a false sense of trust.

After gaining his confidence, Fauzia called the victim to Bijnor. The two stayed at a hotel, where they allegedly had physical relations. Unbeknown to the businessman, the woman secretly recorded an objectionable video, which later became the main tool for blackmail.

Khaki–Khadi Nexus:
Days later, the woman allegedly began threatening the victim with dire consequences, including making the video viral and implicating him in a false rape case. The threats escalated with the entry of other accused, exposing a nexus between the police and political figures.

The accused have been identified as:
Fauzia – the main conspirator who honey-trapped the victim
Adil Zaidi – a Kisan Union member who allegedly used political influence
Shahvez – a local councillor, arrested
Constable Lalu – posted at Kiratpur police station
Constable Puneet Tyagi – posted at Kiratpur police station

₹10 Lakh Extortion Using Police Threats:
The victim alleged that constables Lalu and Puneet Tyagi threatened him with arrest and a false rape case if he failed to comply. The gang allegedly demanded ₹10 lakh in the name of settlement, with councillor Shahvez and Adil Zaidi acting as intermediaries and pressuring the businessman.

Mentally distressed and fearing social disgrace and imprisonment, the victim finally approached the Superintendent of Police directly, narrating how he was being blackmailed by a gang that included serving policemen.

Police Action and Arrests:
Taking the matter seriously, the SP assigned the investigation to CO Najibabad Nitish Pratap. The probe, conducted with technical surveillance and witness statements, found the allegations to be correct.

CO Nitish Pratap stated that the woman, both constables and the political figures were found involved in the blackmailing conspiracy. A case was registered at Kiratpur police station under relevant sections.

Police arrested accused councillor Shahvez and sent him to jail. However, four accused — Fauzia, Adil Zaidi, constable Lalu and constable Puneet Tyagi — are currently absconding. Special teams have been formed to arrest them.

Departmental action, including suspension or dismissal of the two policemen, is also expected.

Police have asserted that strict action will be taken and that those committing crimes in uniform will not be spared.

Note:
This report is based on police statements and the registered FIR. Further investigation is underway, and more details may emerge.

articles.title: Aligarh Woman Ties Drunk Husband to Bed; Mother-in-Law Alleges Threats With Illegal Gun
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A domestic dispute in Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh has taken a dramatic turn after a woman allegedly tied her husband to a bed over his drinking habits, triggering police action following the circulation of a viral video.

body.html:
A domestic dispute in Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh has taken a dramatic turn after a woman allegedly tied her husband to a bed over his drinking habits, triggering police action following the circulation of a viral video.

The incident was reported from Hamidpur village under the Tappal police station area. A video widely shared on social media shows a man tied to a cot, while his wife is heard shouting nearby. According to the family, the woman restrained and allegedly assaulted her husband after accusing him of being drunk.

After the video surfaced, the man’s mother approached the police with a formal complaint. She also submitted a photograph which she claims shows her daughter-in-law holding a country-made pistol. The family has alleged that the woman has been threatening her husband with the illegal firearm.

“My son Pradeep is repeatedly beaten by his wife. She has a pistol and threatens to kill him. Despite searching the house, we could not find the weapon,” the mother alleged, adding that the couple has been married for four years and the harassment has continued for the past two years.

Family members said villagers rushed to the house after learning of the incident and freed the man from the cot. The mother also claimed that earlier complaints to the police and local representatives did not lead to any action.

Police confirmed receiving the complaint and said they are examining the viral video and the allegations related to the firearm. In an official statement, police said Pradeep often quarrels with his wife and neighbours after consuming alcohol, following which his wife tied him to the cot.

Tappal police have summoned the woman for questioning and stated that a detailed investigation is underway to verify all claims, including the alleged possession of an illegal weapon.

articles.title: ‘Lights, Camera, Fake Arrest?’ Viral Video Exposes Serious Misconduct by Aligarh Police
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A serious case of alleged police misconduct has surfaced in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, after a video went viral showing policemen purportedly planting knives on two youths and filming a staged arrest. The video is reportedly from the Panauthi outpost area under Akrabad police station limits.

body.html:
A serious case of alleged police misconduct has surfaced in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, after a video went viral showing policemen purportedly planting knives on two youths and filming a staged arrest.

The video is reportedly from the Panauthi outpost area under Akrabad police station limits. In the footage, police personnel are seen placing knives in the pockets of two young men before recording their arrest, triggering allegations that the youths were falsely portrayed as criminals.

The incident relates to the arrest of Suraj Gautam and Sonu on December 1, 2025, in a mobile phone snatching case. The viral visuals have sparked outrage, with accusations that policemen stabbed themselves or planted weapons to strengthen the case against the accused.

Police Clarification:
In an official statement issued on January 25, 2026, Akrabad police said the viral video is linked to an operation carried out nearly two months ago involving the arrest of two alleged mobile robbers in FIR No. 586/2025 under Sections 304(2) and 317(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police claimed two stolen mobile phones and an illegal knife were recovered during the arrest.

However, to ensure a fair investigation, the policemen seen in the video have been immediately transferred to the police lines. Superintendent of Police (Rural) has been directed to submit an inquiry report within 48 hours.

Area Officer Sanjeev Tomar confirmed that disciplinary action will be taken against the guilty personnel based on the findings of the investigation.

The incident has raised serious questions about police accountability, misuse of power, and the credibility of arrest procedures in the district.
